system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Order: AI, Markets & Geopolitical Hotspots
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system in rapid transition where a technological surge in AI, financial stress in debt and bond markets, and episodic regional wars interact and amplify one another. Great-power management is increasingly performative and transactional, producing limited de‑escalation while regional conflicts (Ukraine, Iran/Middle East) and energy shocks spill into markets and supply chains. Institutional strain—over AI governance, data and critical infrastructure, and cross-border legal/political frictions—is producing cascading policy responses and market volatility.
system_description.scope: State actors, major corporations (tech, finance, energy, defence), global capital markets, critical infrastructure (data centres, energy supply chains), transnational norms/institutions, and active conflict theatres and diplomatic channels.
system_description.super_system: The Anthropocene-era global socio-economic and security system (planetaryized capitalism, transnational technology networks, and interstate order).

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine conflict
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in sustained kinetic and hybrid warfare, with renewed strikes, drone campaigns and sabotage shifting frontlines and sustaining broad European security and economic fallout.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are recalibrating their strategic and economic contest—reengaging on tariffs and bilateral ties while preserving deep competition across supply chains and influence.

variables.name: U.S.–Iran standoff and regional escalation risk
variables.description: The United States and Iran are oscillating between mediated diplomacy and military threats through proxies and direct pressure, maintaining a high risk of wider regional escalation and disruptions to energy flows.

variables.name: Global AI buildout, risk and regulation
variables.description: A rapid commercial and technical surge in artificial intelligence is concentrating corporate power, creating new systemic and safety risks, and prompting an accelerating global push for oversight, liability rules and governance norms.

variables.name: Global bond-market stress and yield re-pricing
variables.description: A sharp, cross-border sell-off in government bonds and a sustained rise in long-term yields is re-pricing risk, straining corporate financing and investment plans and reshaping monetary and fiscal policy space.
